newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Syria has not rejected talks proposals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Syria has not rejected talks proposals.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was still discussing with Syria new U.S.-Israeli proposals for re-launching peace talks between Israel and Syria, and denied that Damascus had rejected them.

"The United States, having had extensive discussions with the Israeli government, is now, on a preliminary basis, sharing some ideas with the Syrian government," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"Some of the stories that I saw in the newspapers this morning, that somehow Syria had rejected these ideas, those stories are false. We are not at the end of that process. We still need to have further discussions," he told reporters.

Israel and the United States worked out the proposals during a visit to Washington earlier this week by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The United States undertook to pass them on to Syria.

But Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said on Thursday Damascus would not agree to fresh talks with Israel unless it honoured all the understandings reached with the previous government under Yitzhak Rabin. Israeli officials have said they would not be bound by all of Rabin's commitments.

At issue is whether Israel will agree to Syria's demand to return all the occupied Golan Heights, as Rabin reportedly promised. The right-wing Netanyahu administration favours a continued Israeli hold on the Golan.
Talks between Syria and the former Labour Party government of Israel were broken off in March, following a series of guerrilla attacks in Israel, and have not resumed.
"The objective here is to see if the United States can help Israel and Syria reach the point where they agree to recommence their political discussions towards peace in the Middle East.
U.S. officials said special Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross was considering a fresh trip to the Middle East, but had made no final decision.
Burns confirmed reports from Damascus that a message from U.S. President Bill Clinton had been delivered to the Syrian government. He did not disclose its details.
